scope: Current foundation choices across all 16 canonical layers. Reasons describe fit for the accepted native workload, not universal superiority. This is a reconciliation of pinned source reviews and retained executions at base fb04bf702ea67b14163405f0ebe132e393ebbd8a; it performs no new installation, model run or comparative benchmark. Selected means retained for its stated role, not mandatory activation in every task. Unqualified and conditional alternatives have not failed a test merely because they are not adopted.

layers.title: Native clients
layers.requirement: Run coding and bounded research with existing native accounts, client tools, model choices and resumable sessions.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude Code; application SDKs only for a demonstrated application requirement.
layers.rationale: Both clients have returned native source-task and continuation evidence and preserve the existing account and tool surfaces. Replacing them with an API framework adds an application-owned runtime without a demonstrated gap in these bounded tasks.
limitations: The recorded tasks do not establish a comparative model-quality ranking or causal provider savings.
Same-session continuation does not establish every crash, provider cancellation or cross-host recovery condition.
layers.overturn_when: A required structured-event, custom-tool or application state capability is unavailable through the native path and a supported SDK implementation passes the same task, account, effect and recovery checks.

candidates.name: Codex
candidates.rationale: Actual native tasks and session recovery exist; retain native account, tools and model selection.

candidates.name: Claude Code
candidates.rationale: Native task, interactive usage/HUD and manual compaction observations qualify the current client path within their recorded scope.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Fits an application-owned API agent; it is not a substitute for the established subscription-backed native Codex account and behavior.

candidates.name: Claude Agent SDK
candidates.rationale: Use when application orchestration specifically needs its supported structured interface and authentication route; no current bounded-task replacement need was demonstrated.

candidates.name: Letta Code
candidates.rationale: A separate memory-aware coding architecture is credible, but its task quality and migration costs have not been compared against these native clients.

candidates.name: MCPorter native bridge
candidates.rationale: Supporting CLI bridge for scoped native MCP calls and retained daemon connections; it does not replace client accounts, hooks or the agent loop.

layers.title: Instructions and skills
layers.requirement: Give each task concise canonical rules and useful upstream procedures without activating whole instruction or plugin catalogs.
layers.current_choice: Selected ECC search-first/iterative-retrieval skills, native project instructions, on-demand references and the optional Agent Skills reference validator; task-selected TypeSafe, gh-fix-ci and security-best-practices for Codex/Claude.
layers.rationale: The two selected ECC skills have recorded matching hashes and native discovery. Their bounded roles fit existing practice; importing complete hooks, rules or agent packs creates overlapping policies without measured benefit. Selected upstream additions address semantic context propagation and focused CI/security guidance; installation, native use and comparative superiority remain separate.
limitations: The community-practice review records no measured task-quality improvement or provider-cost change.
Reference format validation does not establish support for every client extension or successful activation.
layers.overturn_when: A specific task exposes a missing procedure, and a pinned candidate works in native discovery and task execution with less conflict or better measured results than the current procedure.

candidates.name: ECC selected skills
candidates.rationale: Reuse the two accepted on-demand skills. The whole hooks/rules bundle is not selected, and its older fixed-thinking/model guidance is not imported.

candidates.name: Agent Skills reference tools

candidates.name: VoltAgent subagent collection
candidates.rationale: Role discovery is useful, but the existing bounded native workers already cover current work; broad agent imports have no demonstrated advantage.

candidates.rationale: Installed for both clients; fresh advisory triage matched 7/8 frozen labels. Preserve the insufficient-versus-contradicted disagreement, recover original evidence and keep exact rules in code. No automatic ranking, execution authority or general accuracy win.

candidates.rationale: The maintained CI helper passed its clean-check path on PR55. Optional security guidance adds framework controls beyond secret/workflow scanners, with version-sensitive advice and finding quality still requiring qualification.

layers.title: Workers and task ownership
layers.requirement: Delegate bounded independent work, preserve owned edits and actual failed results, and integrate only after relevant review.
layers.current_choice: Native Claude/Codex workers with owned Worktrunk worktrees; Beads for a real dependency queue, optional qualified cross-client review and an opt-in semantic-evidence-reviewer with explicit TypeSafe context.
layers.rationale: Native writing, review and selected-child recovery have returned evidence without another orchestration runtime. Worktrunk's actual old/new comparison corrected child working-directory behavior. Durable cross-host effects would require a different acceptance boundary.
limitations: Graceful native Workflow resume is separate from the systemd child-crash fixture; neither transfers every hard-crash guarantee to the other.
The restricted reviewer tool profile is not the accepted inherited-tool lane. The older companion backend acceptance does not certify every outer plugin invocation.
Native model/effort settings are inherited and returned identities recorded. Skill propagation is not a universal runtime/model ranking; account scopes and failed read paths remain evidence.
layers.overturn_when: A real task needs durable multi-host state, approval waits or effect recovery beyond native workers, and one challenger passes frozen cancellation, replay, ownership and integration cases.

candidates.name: Claude native workers
candidates.rationale: Owned native children and graceful workflow recovery have actual retained results; use the qualified role/tool configuration.

layers.title: Isolation
layers.requirement: Separate edits and apply a real filesystem/network boundary only where the selected task requires enforced restrictions.
layers.current_choice: Worktrunk/Git worktrees for edit ownership, sandbox-runtime for qualified Linux restrictions, and platform-specific Apple Container use only on an eligible host.
layers.rationale: These mechanisms cover different requirements: worktrees separate changes, while accepted sandbox profiles enforce selected access rules. A managed VM or OCI platform adds a separate deployment boundary that the bounded native workload does not currently need.
limitations: A worktree is not a security sandbox. Ordinary native or Dagu processes are not automatically sandboxed.
Selected access/network fixtures do not certify hostile workloads, resource limits or unsupported platforms.
layers.overturn_when: Untrusted code or a deployment target requires a stronger VM/OCI boundary, and the selected alternative passes workload, network, resource, cleanup and host compatibility checks.

candidates.name: Worktrunk
candidates.rationale: Native worktree lifecycle evidence supports separate writing ownership without claiming security isolation.

candidates.name: sandbox-runtime
candidates.rationale: Retain the small installed native layer with explicit accepted read/write/network profiles before operating another sandbox service.

candidates.name: Apple Container
candidates.rationale: A platform-specific volume/container case is accepted; it is not a portable replacement for the Linux/WSL profile.

candidates.name: gVisor
candidates.rationale: A stronger OCI application-kernel boundary is relevant for hostile container code, but needs an OCI workload and separate platform acceptance absent from the current native path.

candidates.name: E2B
candidates.rationale: A separate VM and managed lifecycle can fit untrusted generated research code; no current requirement or comparative acceptance justifies substituting it for local scoped execution.

candidates.name: Docker Engine / Moby
candidates.rationale: Useful when an upstream image or reproducible OCI deployment closes a dependency/runtime gap. No matched result shows better reproduction or recovery than the accepted native services for this workload.

candidates.name: Podman / Quadlet
candidates.rationale: A maintained rootless OCI challenger with systemd-oriented Quadlet management. Image, networking, volume, GPU and Docker-API compatibility remain workload-specific and unmeasured here.

layers.title: Code navigation
layers.requirement: Retrieve exact source and references for changes with a conceptual or structural index only when it answers the actual question.
layers.current_choice: Focused source reads, Serena symbols, ast-grep, scoped codebase-memory and jCodeMunch; SocratiCode handles conceptual search in the semantic layer.
layers.rationale: The selected lanes have scoped exact-retrieval/native-client evidence and distinct roles. Another code graph is not preferred merely for advertised speed; known source can be cheaper than an indexed round trip.
limitations: Compressed structure and symbol indexes omit implementation details; correctness still requires original source.
No representative cross-repository or cross-language benchmark establishes a global best code retriever.
layers.overturn_when: A sealed task set in the target languages shows a challenger returning more correct source/references at an acceptable total indexing, retrieval and maintenance cost.

candidates.name: Serena
candidates.rationale: Accepted symbol-body/reference retrieval fits exact edits and complements conceptual search.

candidates.name: ast-grep
candidates.rationale: Native structural matching is retained for syntax-shaped questions that exact text search does not express.

candidates.name: codebase-memory-mcp
candidates.rationale: The accepted scoped static graph covers selected gaps in language-server support; avoid redundant full indexes.

candidates.name: jCodeMunch
candidates.rationale: Exact indexed retrieval and both-client acceptance support bounded use. Its bytes-avoided estimate is not provider savings.

candidates.name: CodeGraph
candidates.rationale: A credible local semantic-graph alternative; its speed/completeness claims need a target-language comparison before replacing the accepted symbol and graph lanes.

layers.title: Documents and ingestion
layers.requirement: Find source-grounded Markdown/document content with controlled ingestion and retrieve the original body before relying on a result.
layers.current_choice: Scoped QMD BM25; Context Hub for selected developer docs; MarkItDown HTML and Poppler PDF conversion in their accepted scopes.
layers.rationale: QMD's 12-query diagnostic gave BM25 and hybrid equal recall@3/5 with reported average latency of 5 ms versus 10,328 ms. This supports the simple default on that workload. Lightweight accepted conversion precedes a larger OCR/layout platform.
limitations: The QMD diagnostic used one ordered run and an incompletely sealed expanded index; it is not a general retrieval ranking.
HTML/PDF fixtures do not qualify arbitrary Office documents, scans, tables or filing layouts. Context Hub's retained size comparison grew by 85 tokens.
layers.overturn_when: A sealed representative corpus/query set shows useful quality gains with acceptable repeated end-to-end latency, or layout/OCR failures justify a separately qualified parser.

candidates.name: QMD BM25
candidates.rationale: Native search/get works and the retained four-mode diagnostic did not justify hybrid's greater latency. Equal recall in one run does not prove universal dominance.

candidates.name: Context Hub
candidates.rationale: Retain selected upstream documentation retrieval; the measured artifact grew by 85 tokens, so selection rests on useful content rather than guaranteed compression.

candidates.name: MarkItDown
candidates.rationale: The installed lightweight HTML lane passed its selected conversion; do not infer uninstalled extras or OCR acceptance.

candidates.name: Poppler
candidates.rationale: Retain the separate native PDF fixture evidence without extending it to every scanned or table-heavy document.

candidates.name: Docling
candidates.rationale: Preferred source-reviewed layout candidate when a real filing/layout requirement exceeds lightweight conversion; target-document quality must be measured first.

candidates.name: LlamaIndex
candidates.rationale: Targeted connectors can close an ingestion gap; a broad dependency bundle is not needed for current scoped Markdown retrieval.

layers.title: Semantic code retrieval
layers.requirement: Answer conceptual code questions using a scoped local index and a compatible embedding service, with recoverable state.
layers.current_choice: SocratiCode, Qdrant and the accepted vLLM/Nemotron embedding runtime; use exact source navigation after retrieval.
layers.rationale: The existing watcher, actual embedding inference, selected queries and restored state are qualified together. Replacing a working vector store or server has no demonstrated advantage on this project's workload.
limitations: Four paired upstream examples first-ranked correctly establish compatibility, not a held-out domain or cross-model benchmark.
The vLLM compatibility pin is host-specific; the retained newer-version initialization failure is not a failure of other serving repositories.
layers.overturn_when: A sealed project/domain retrieval set shows improved source-grounded quality and acceptable latency, memory and lifecycle costs, or a supported target model cannot run in the current service.

candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted automatic project index and conceptual query path rather than duplicate it with another graph/search service.

candidates.name: Haystack

candidates.name: Hugging Face Hub native CLI
candidates.rationale: Supporting native discovery and revision-pinned model download path with retained local model provenance. This selects artifact acquisition, not a best embedding or serving model.

Bounded sanitized assistant excerpts are not complete transcripts, and exact lifetime memory token savings are unknown.

candidates.name: Claude-mem

layers.title: Context and usage efficiency
layers.requirement: Supply useful task context with recoverable originals and measure artifact reductions separately from provider usage.
layers.current_choice: Focused reads and scoped retrieval first; RTK, Context Mode, guarded Headroom, explicit-file Repomix and TOON only for suitable artifacts; ccusage observes native usage.

TOON expands the full catalog relative to compact JSON; guarded compression must return originals on rejection. Exact whole-PC lifetime savings are unmeasured.

layers.title: Quality and evaluation

layers.title: CI and supply chain

layers.title: Recovery and portability
layers.requirement: Reproduce selected tools and recover actual application state on an explicitly adopted host without copying authentication stores or treating old receipts as new acceptance.
layers.current_choice: Owned native install/rollback recipes, existing uv lock-based adoption, Restic and application-native backups, and qualified native session resume.
layers.rationale: Retained clean-prefix installs, independent restores and selected hosted/guest cases support the native recipe approach. A broader environment platform is not justified for reproducing an already locked bounded SDK/tool profile.
limitations: Synthetic off-host/guest cases and a clean hosted runner do not certify the new physical PC, GPU, secrets or all application state.
Native sign-ins and host-specific acceptance remain necessary; rollback and hash checks alone do not prove a model task or service recovery.
layers.overturn_when: A real multi-language/system dependency or state-loss case exceeds the selected recipes, and the proposed environment/backup alternative passes install, restore, resume and cleanup on the target host.

candidates.name: Restic
candidates.rationale: Actual scoped file/application restore and independent output checks support reuse; preserve every receipt's same-host, hosted or synthetic boundary.

candidates.name: Litestream
candidates.rationale: Continuous SQLite replication could close a real recovery-point requirement; the reviewed version adds a source-database lock and a replica operating policy. Native online backup plus Restic already meets the bounded accepted restore need.

candidates.name: uv
candidates.rationale: The existing native Python layer reproduces accepted versions from hash-bearing locks in an isolated environment without a new manager.

candidates.name: mise
candidates.rationale: Multi-language tool/version management can help a broader bootstrap; it adds no demonstrated requirement beyond current uv-based adoption.

candidates.name: chezmoi
candidates.rationale: Can manage selected non-secret configuration and drift; do not turn it into blanket home-directory or native authentication-store capture.

candidates.name: Devbox
candidates.rationale: A Nix-backed environment closure changes the host model and overlaps the accepted native lock; no target-host comparison establishes a benefit.

candidates.name: Determinate Nix installer
candidates.rationale: A privileged system-platform installation is not required for the current native/WSL adoption profile; it remains a separate lane if a Nix requirement is explicitly selected.

layers.title: Observation and optional inference
layers.requirement: Observe real native usage/service outcomes through one privacy-filtered local pipeline and qualify any optional model route on its actual workload.
layers.current_choice: OTel Collector Contrib, Prometheus/Loki/Grafana, Alertmanager/ntfy, scoped AgentsView/otel-tui and the native Claude HUD; inference/gateway trials retain separate qualification.
layers.rationale: Real native histories, current telemetry, rendered dashboards and an observed HUD already answer the selected operational questions. Another hook/trace collection stack would duplicate data processing unless it answers a concrete missing trace or evaluation question.
limitations: Source time differs from scrape time; usage differs from savings. The current interactive HUD evidence does not certify every statistic or automatic compaction.
Local generation and gateway acceptance are route/workload-specific; catalog presence is not a passed exact-model task.
layers.overturn_when: A required trace, evaluation or supported model/hardware workload is unanswerable by the current path, and one alternative passes privacy, fidelity, latency/cost and recovery comparisons without duplicate capture.

candidates.name: OTel Collector Contrib
candidates.rationale: One native collector supplies the accepted privacy transform and metrics/log outputs for both clients; the core collector is a source dependency, not a second process.

candidates.name: Prometheus
candidates.rationale: Actual native metrics and rule evaluation are qualified, with process writers kept distinguishable.

candidates.name: Loki
candidates.rationale: The accepted privacy-filtered log store complements Prometheus without treating raw conversation capture as required telemetry.

candidates.name: Grafana
candidates.rationale: Rendered panels were checked against actual native service results; this is operational observation, not model-quality evaluation.

candidates.name: Alertmanager
candidates.rationale: Retained local grouping/routing evidence complements Prometheus rules, within the accepted loopback receiver scope.

candidates.name: ntfy
candidates.rationale: An inspectable local alert sink and corrected templates serve the current notification chain without implying external messaging setup.

candidates.name: AgentsView
candidates.rationale: Scoped native archive refresh and observation work; titles/bodies remain private and automatic discovery retains its original limits.

candidates.name: otel-tui
candidates.rationale: Accepted bounded local trace inspection provides a small terminal lane without another standing web analytics service.

candidates.name: Claude HUD
candidates.rationale: Later native interactive evidence observed model/project/context/usage rendering, superseding the older dialog-only observation for that exact scope.

candidates.name: OpenLIT
candidates.rationale: Coding-agent instrumentation exists, but adding another hook/trace collector duplicates current collection unless a missing trace question warrants it.

candidates.name: Phoenix
candidates.rationale: A first trace-analysis candidate if current receipts become unwieldy; no measured need supports an additional trace UI now.

candidates.name: SGLang
candidates.rationale: A credible serving alternative when the current engine cannot meet a supported model/hardware workload; no such comparative win is retained for this host.

candidates.name: llama.cpp optional local inference
candidates.rationale: Retain the pinned GGUF/CUDA trial for the qualified partial-offload planner repair. One RTX4090 task does not replace hosted native agents, establish broad quality, or qualify every hardware/model combination.
